what: The exact revision of each standard this site was built against. Proposal §2: it converts 'which version of the spec does this page describe?' from a thing someone remembers into a thing the build reads. src/loaders/spec-source.mjs reads this file; nothing in src/ hardcodes a version string, and tests/spec-source.test.mjs asserts that.

specifications.name: Agent Plugins

supersedes.where: Quoted in design/starlight-site-proposal.md line 249, as an illustration of what agentplugins/agent-plugins-site pins in its own specification-source.json.
supersedes.why: Recorded rather than adopted. It is a real commit and it resolves, but it is 13 days behind the revision this site was actually built against, and nobody on this project consulted it. Copying it would have produced a provenance record naming a commit no measurement here ever touched -- a correct-looking sha attributed to the wrong source. The pin above is the one that was verified at measurement time.

specifications.note: 1.0.0 is the Published version and the one every plugin in this catalog targets in its own plugin.json $schema URL. spec/1.1.0.md also exists upstream and is a Working Draft; it is not pinned here because nothing in this catalog targets it. Both commit fields above are 40-hex object names, never branch names: a pin to a moving ref verifies forever and means something different each time.

specifications.name: Agent Skills

version.reason: The Agent Skills specification declares no version of itself. There is no version upstream to pin, so this key is omitted rather than filled. Absent is not the same as unknown and neither is the same as a placeholder: proposal §12, 'Missing metadata shows as absent, not stubbed.'
version.predicate: In agentskills/agentskills at commit 69ef37e9424c0a7ea9dd2293b559e43ec8176379: (1) grep -rni version docs/ returns only SVG XML declarations and prose about version control; (2) grep -rnoE '[0-9]+[.][0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?' docs/specification.mdx returns 1.0, 2.0, 3.14 and 1.0 at lines 50, 53, 139 and 159, every one of them inside an EXAMPLE skill frontmatter block, i.e. an example value of a skill author's own metadata.version field and not a version of the specification; (3) a wrap-insensitive window scan, tr '\n' ' ' < docs/specification.mdx | grep -oiE '.{40}version.{40}', returns the same two example blocks, confirming (2) is not a line-wrap artifact.
version.positiveControl: TWO CONTROLS AT DIFFERENT LEVELS, and the weaker one is named as weak. (A) LEVEL 2, PARTIAL: the identical needle, grep -rni version, run against agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec, returns 'Spec Version: 1.0.0' at spec/1.0.0.md:3. This proves the selector is not dead. IT DOES NOT PROVE THE SELECTOR FINDS THE CLASS, and the difference is not academic: a version declared as 'spec-level: 2.1' or 'revision: 3' survives the word-needle entirely AND leaves this control green, because the search and its control are the same needle and share its vocabulary by construction. Verified by running the needle against exactly that decoy: it returns nothing while the agent-plugins control still passes. (B) LEVEL 2, LOAD-BEARING, AND THIS IS THE ONE THE ABSENCE RESTS ON: predicate (2) is vocabulary-independent -- it matches the SHAPE of a version, not the word -- and it returns a NON-EMPTY set on the document under test rather than a zero on a different document. Re-measured at commit 69ef37e9: four hits, 2.0/1.0/3.14/1.0 at lines 50/53/139/159, each one dispositioned individually as example skill-author frontmatter. Same needle on agent-plugins at ff8ab5e3 returns 1.0.0 at spec/1.0.0.md:3. The conclusion is therefore an EXHAUSTIVE ENUMERATION WITH EVERY HIT ACCOUNTED FOR, which is a stronger object than an absence, because there is no zero in it to be produced by a dead selector.
version.doNotUse: skills-ref/pyproject.toml in the same repository declares version = 0.1.0. That is the version of the REFERENCE LIBRARY, which the specification itself describes as 'for demonstration purposes only. It is not meant to be used in production.' It is not the specification's version and must not be pinned here.

status.reason: The Agent Skills specification declares no publication status of itself. Omitted for the same reason as version.
status.predicate: TWO PREDICATES, because the first one alone rests on a word. (1) NEEDLE: grep -rni status docs/specification.mdx docs/home.mdx README.md in agentskills/agentskills at commit 69ef37e9424c0a7ea9dd2293b559e43ec8176379 returns zero lines. (2) ENUMERATION, which is what the absence actually rests on: a status has no recognisable SHAPE the way a version number does, so no vocabulary-independent needle exists for it and searching harder cannot close the class. Enumerate instead of searching. The entire self-describing frontmatter of docs/specification.mdx at 69ef37e9 is two keys, title and description -- awk '/^---$/{n++; next} n==1' docs/specification.mdx | grep -oE '^[a-zA-Z_-]+:' | sort -u. Whatever a publication status might be CALLED, it would have to be one of those two keys, and neither is one. The one remaining path, a status stated in body prose rather than in metadata, is closed by inspection: the document opens directly on '## Directory structure' with no title block, no preamble and no front matter beyond those two keys.
status.positiveControl: LEVEL 2, AND IT CONTROLS THE ENUMERATION RATHER THAN THE NEEDLE. In agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec at ff8ab5e3, spec/1.0.0.md declares BOTH facts in a body header block in its first five lines: '**Spec Version: 1.0.0**' at line 3 and '**Status: Published**' at line 5. So a specification that does state its status states it exactly where this enumeration looks, in the opening block, and the enumeration would have found it. That is the property that matters -- not merely that a needle fires somewhere, but that the method would have caught the thing in the place it actually occurs. The needle-on-a-different-document control is retained as corroboration and is explicitly NOT the load-bearing one: it shares its vocabulary with the search it guards, so a status recorded as 'Stage: Draft' or 'Maturity: stable' would survive it while leaving it green.

specifications.note: The Agent Skills format was originally developed by Anthropic, released as an open standard, and has been adopted by a growing number of agent products. That is the standard's own wording, from its README, and it is quoted rather than paraphrased on /about/standards/.
